The ntp object is system managed and cannot be manually added or deleted; access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. The third settable attribute is assignment-method, with values manual, dhcp and both (default both), which selects whether the system uses manually configured values, DHCP-supplied values, or both. Verify with 'show ntp ntp-enabled ntp-auth-enabled ntp-active-server assignment-method'; ntp-active-server reports the currently active NTP server. Authentication also needs an ntp-key and an ntp-server with auth-key-id set.

NTP keys are created with 'add ntp-key-<key-id> key-type <value> key-value <value> [is-trusted <value>]' and maintained with the matching set, show and delete forms. key-type is the hash algorithm for NTP message digest computation and accepts sha-1, aes-cmac, sha-256 and md5; there is no default, so it is mandatory on add. key-id is a number in the range 1..65534. key-value is a string of length 8..40. is-trusted marks the key as a trusted NTP key and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: 'add ntp-key-2 is-trusted true key-type sha-1 key-value Infinera'.

Yes. The ntp-server origin attribute is the NTP address assignment method: dhcp means the address was assigned to this system by a DHCP server, manual means it was manually configured, and the guide states that a user can convert a DHCP-configured NTP entry into a manually configured one by changing this attribute. Run 'set ntp-server-<ip-address> origin manual'. The default for origin is manual. The same command also carries auth-key-id (uint32 or not-applicable, default not-applicable), label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance, default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed). The ip-address key accepts IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use 'show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>', for example 'show ntp-server-status-172.19.13.218'. The key attribute is reach, an 8-bit shift register holding the reachability of the configured server with the most recent probe in the 2^0 position; the value 377 indicates that all the recent probes have been answered. Supporting attributes are when (seconds elapsed since the last packet was received), poll (polling interval in seconds), delay, offset and jitter (all in milliseconds), stratum of the remote peer, refid (reference clock type or address), type (local, unicast, multicast or broadcast), auth-status (ok, yes, bad or none, default none) and condition, whose values include sys.peer, reject and candidate.

'restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>]' takes type cold, warm or shutdown, and if <type> is not provided a warm start is done by default. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes; a cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost, while a cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting. warm reboots only the processor of the CHM6, UCM4 and similar and is non service affecting, again regaining connectivity within five minutes; on XMM4 it is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. If <resource-id> is omitted the active node controller card is restarted. The command prompts for confirmation unless -f is given. Not all cards support all restart types; cards support cold, warm and shutdown, card sub-components cold and warm, and toms cold only.

'set-time' is only applicable when time-source is manual, that is when NTP is not enabled. If NTP is running the node takes its time from the server and the manual set is rejected. Check with 'show clock time-source' (values ntp and manual, default manual) and, if needed, disable NTP with 'set ntp ntp-enabled false'. The syntax is 'set-time [new-time=]<value>' in Operational Mode, and the value is in a format derived from ISO 8601 with combined date and time, such as 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z, where Z represents UTC; a non-UTC timezone is allowed by giving +/-hh:mm instead of Z, for example 'set-time 2021-04-01T18:46:44+03:00'. Retrieve the current time with the 'time' command, which reports it in the system configured timezone rather than the timezone used in the set-time command.

Yes, 'status equipment'. The Equipment dashboard summarises all equipment in the system together with relevant details such as temperature sensors and power values. It lists the chassis, the cards per chassis with their subtype, the toms per card, and generic status per entity: presence or absence, oper-state and alarms. The default scope is the entire network element. For large NEs you can filter per chassis by giving the chassis id as a parameter, for example 'status equipment 5'; only existing chassis ids are accepted and wildcards are not supported, so either all chassis are displayed or exactly one. Full syntax is 'status [[dashboard=]<system | equipment | L0-oxcon | L0-ocm | L1-traffic>] [[filter=]<value>]', access is Operational Mode. In the output a check mark means oper-state enabled, a cross means oper-state disabled and a padlock means admin-locked.

Use 'clear [-f] system [[action=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>]'. The type parameter selects the mode: factory-reset resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing respective files and user configurations, which may imply loss of connectivity; full-wipe cleans the entire system and reinstalls the SW on the controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, and requires a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover; inactive clears the inactive software partition. target is the entire system or a specific chassis or card AID, and if no target is given the entire system is cleared. restart-behavior is a standard restart (default) or shutdown, in which case the system does not restart after the clear. Restrictions: factory-reset does not take effect on G30 Optical Carrier-Cards OCC2T and OCC2E but is supported on the G30 controller card FRCU, and 'clear system factory-reset' with the shutdown option is not supported on L0 cards; full-wipe is not supported on G30 line cards CHM1R and UTM2 or on OCC2T/OCC2E and currently takes effect on FRCU only. For a simple database wipe use 'clear database'. -f forces the command without confirmation.

Run the 'time' command. It takes no parameters and simply displays the system's time, and it is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The output is a single ISO 8601 style timestamp, for example 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00. It reports the time based on the system configured timezone. For more detail, 'show clock' returns current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source, DST-active and last-time-jump.

The 'uptime' command displays the system uptime and load average and takes no parameters; access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether there are multiple tasks queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the system (card), and the load average number itself. The rule given is that a load average value is considered to be high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card. Example output: '21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39'.

Yes. 'manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value>' takes the AID of the object to be switched and warns before acting: 'Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]'. You confirm at that prompt to proceed, or pass -f to force the command without confirmation. Access is Operational Mode. The resource is the controller card AID, for example 'manual-switchover card-1-3' on a 1830 GX G42 chassis, 'manual-switchover card-1-5' on a G32 chassis, and 'manual-switchover card-1-12' on a G34c chassis. The full procedure is in the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

'show protection' displays the protection container. It is a show-only command with no parameters, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Below it, the individual objects have their own commands: 'show protection-group-<name>' for a protection group and its attributes such as pg-state, pg-request, switching-mode, reversion-mode, hold-off-timer, wtr-timer, remaining-wtr, working-pu, protection-pu and last-switch-trigger, and 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>' for a member unit's state and role.

On protection-group the switching-mode attribute takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. The wait-to-restore timer is wtr-timer: it is the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, with a range of 60..720 seconds and a default of 300 seconds. It is only applicable in revertive mode, and reversion-mode itself takes revertive or non-revertive and defaults to non-revertive, so you must set reversion-mode revertive for the WTR timer to apply. The related read-only remaining-wtr shows the remaining time, range 0..720 seconds. The separate hold-off-timer is the switching trigger soaking time before switching, in 1-millisecond steps, range 0..10000 ms, default 0. Set them with 'set protection-group-<name> switching-mode bidirectional wtr-timer 600'.

Use the operating command 'protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>' in Operational Mode. operation-type takes force, lockout, manual or release; switch-target is the target of the switch and is not needed for the release and lockout operations. The guide's example is 'protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection'. -f forces the command without confirmation. The same effect can be configured on the group itself through pg-request on protection-group, whose values are clear (the default), manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise applies only to bidirectional SNCP).

Read the protection unit's state: 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> state role'. state is the state of the protection-unit and takes active, standby, available or unknown, so the member showing active is the one carrying traffic. role identifies the unit as working or protection. The show form also returns AID, transport-entity (the instance identifier of the transport entity), alarm-report-control and label. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. At the group level, 'show protection-group-<name> pg-state last-switch-trigger' tells you why the group is in its current position; the AID form is <protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>, for example test/1-6-T1.

Most alarms have both an automatic raise criteria and a clear criteria, but a very small subset have no clear criteria and instead require the user to acknowledge and clear them manually. Those are identified in the alarm inventory by can-be-cleared-by-user = true, which you can list with 'show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true'. Clear them with 'clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*]', for example 'clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL'; -f forces the command without confirmation. Access is Operational Mode. Note that this mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource but with the system itself, that is system wide or global alarms.

That is governed by the system-wide arc-behavior switch on alarm-control. 'set alarm-control arc-behavior <value>' takes leave-alarms or clear-alarms and defaults to leave-alarms. With leave-alarms, when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are left in a raised mode; with clear-alarms, setting ARC to inhibit clears the current alarms. So by default already-raised alarms stay up. Check the setting with 'show alarm-control'. The same object carries alarm-soaking-behavior, with values automatic (soaking time as defined in the FM profile) and no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile have no soaking time), default automatic; the OSC LOF alarm instead uses the per-facility user-configurable lof-soak-timer on the PBAx card. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use 'show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type>', for example 'show alarm-inventory-TIM' or 'show alarm-inventory-MSIM'. The alarm inventory holds all possible alarm types for the system with static information for each one. The attributes are alarm-type-description, a description of the alarm type (string 0..128); corrective-action, system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered this alarm (string 0..256); alarm-category, one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security; default-severity, the list of possible default severities (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event), since the same alarm may have different defaults per resource-type; resource-type; and service-affecting, one of indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. alarm-severity-entry configures the severity for one particular alarm on one particular resource type. The syntax is 'set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> [severity <value>]', for example 'set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor' or 'set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major'. resource-type is the type to be modified (CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31 and so on), alarm-type is the abbreviated alarm code (ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD and so on), direction is na, ingress or egress, and location is na, near-end or far-end. severity accepts critical, event, major, minor, not-reported and warning. Read it back with 'show alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity service-affecting'; service-affecting shows indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted. Press '?' after the command to list available entities.

They set the same severity values but address different things. 'set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>' modifies a named profile entry, for example 'set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical', and 'show alarm-severity-profile' displays the profiles; press '?' after 'set alarm-severity-profile' to list the available profiles. alarm-severity-entry instead targets one specific combination, keyed as <resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location>, for example 'set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor', and its show form also returns service-affecting. Both objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted, and both are available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use 'show current-alarms', which shows the list of currently raised alarms, and read its two attributes: number-of-alarms, the number of currently raised alarms, and last-changed, the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, meaning either a raise or a clear event. So 'show current-alarms number-of-alarms last-changed' gives the count and the age of the list in one line. Access is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. The system dashboard from the 'status' command also prints an alarm summary with the number of alarms broken down per severity, for example '13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor)'.

Look at the conditions with the 'get-conditions' command. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as 'not-reported' or 'not-alarmed', when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. The syntax is 'get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]'. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID are free filters with no default. Access is Operational Mode.

Use the operational-mode command set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). state is mandatory and takes an operator-state value of none, ack or close. Use all-alarms to set every currently raised alarm, or alarm-id-list to name from 1 up to 10 alarm ids (leafref). acknowledge-text is optional and stores a string of length 0..256 in the alarm itself. Setting an alarm to the state it already has is accepted, with only the text being updated. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example, or set-alarm-state ack 28872914984089790,17580406225060810165.

Yes: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*, in Operational Mode. target is an instance-identifier naming the objects that will have their event counter statistics cleared. Currently the only supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Clear every AAA server with clear statistics aaa-server, or a single one with clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation and -h displays help.

Use show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. -n=x displays only the last x entries and -t gives an aligned table instead of the default CSV output, for example show -n=5 log security -t. If the table becomes too wide, drop columns with exclude=<column> after the logname (tab auto-complete lists the removable columns), and post-process with piped commands, e.g. show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Valid logname values are messages, linecard, shell-command, netconf-command, apps, cli-command, alarm, configuration, kernel, user, event, security and ztp. Access mode is Operational, and Candidate Configuration for the show command only. Note that due to system restrictions the security log may not be cleared.

Yes, that is expected: console logging is off by default. The log-console attribute enabled (values true, false) defaults to false. Switch it on with set log-console enabled true, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode, and verify with show log-console. The other log-console attribute is source-facilities, the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration: all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1, local2, local3, local4, local5, local6, local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level, uucp. Severity filtering is then done with log-console-facility-filter.

Add a log-console-facility-filter: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where <name> identifies a single syslog facility or all of them if it is 'all'. severity takes emergency (level 0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, default equals-or-higher. So to keep only serious messages: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical', which with the default equals-or-higher passes critical, alert and emergency. set, show and delete use the same key. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

It is set per log file with log-file. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained: uint8, range 1..20, default 10. When rotating files because max size is reached, the oldest files are discarded once the total number exceeds this value. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes: uint8, range 1..30, default 30. So a default file holds 10 files of 30 MB, and the largest possible history is 20 files of 30 MB. Change them with add/set log-file-<name> number-of-files <value> max-file-size <value>. Other attributes are source-facilities (default all), pattern-match (regex, string 0..255) and sensitive-data (none, both, only). The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted.

Yes. Restrict the file's source-facilities to the authentication facility (facility 4, used for authentication/authorization attempt messages), then optionally add a severity filter. For example: add log-file-authlog source-facilities authentication, then add log-file-facility-filter-authlog/authentication severity <value> compare-op <value>. The filter key is add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name>, where the filter name is one syslog facility or 'all'. severity values are emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational (default) and debug; compare-op values are equals, equals-or-higher (default) and not-equals. Note the log-file source-facilities default is all, so it must be set explicitly to authentication.

Configure the collector with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... transport <udp|tls|tcp> port <value>. Unless you say otherwise, transport is udp (so tls must be set explicitly), port is 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format is rfc5424, the alternative being rfc3164. Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual (or dhcp), source-facilities all, destination-facility-override disabled (otherwise a facility number in range 0..11 or 16..23), sensitive-data none (also only, both) and alarm-report-control allowed. name is a string 0...64, address may be IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name, and pattern-match is a regular expression string 0..255. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes, per collector, but it can only narrow. Use add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The filter is based on the log-server source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the configured source facilities, so it cannot widen what the server sends; to add a facility you must change the log-server source-facilities. The filter name identifies one syslog facility (kernel, user-level, mail-system, system-daemons, authentication, syslog-internal, line-printer, network-news, uucp, clock-daemon-9, security, ftp-daemon, ntp, log-audit, log-alert, clock-daemon-15, local0..local7) or 'all'. severity defaults to informational, compare-op to equals-or-higher (also equals, not-equals). Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug.

set syslog remote-logging-switch false. That flag, when false, disables all remote logging destinations while leaving the configured log-server entries in place; it defaults to true. Check it with show syslog remote-logging-switch. Access: Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Related syslog attributes and defaults: source-address (default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (true), log-relay, which enables remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller (default false), assignment-method both/manual/dhcp (default both), niap-compliant-logging (false), privacy-mode, the GDRP filter (false), alarm-report-control (allowed) and label (string 0..256).

The aaa-server shared-secret attribute is documented as String (length 0...128) with default sharedkey, and it is displayed as * when shown. The command note states that the maximum length of shared-secret is 64 characters, and any value more than 64 characters is denied with an error message, so 64 is the practical limit. Set it with add aaa-server-<server-name> ... shared-secret <value> or set aaa-server-<server-name> shared-secret <value>, in Operational or Candidate Configuration Mode. The server-name itself is a string of length 1...64.

No, that is expected behaviour. show aaa-statistics-<server-name> authentication-requests displays the number of authentication requests, and the guide notes that for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP: the authentication requests counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. aaa-statistics applies only to AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol. The other counters are connection-failures (which includes failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts), authentication-rejects, authorization-requests, authorization-rejects and accounting-requests. Reset them with clear statistics aaa-server-<name>.

The ACE action attribute defaults to drop, so an unspecified match is dropped; the permitted values are drop, accept and reject. Syntax: add ace-<name>/<sequence-id> [action <value>] [direction <value>] [protocol <value>] .... Pre-condition: an ACL must be in place before an ACE can be added, and at least one of source IP, destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. sequence-id range is 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface; use multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified, and adding another such ACE beyond 16 returns an error. Other defaults: direction input, protocol any, ttl 255, logging-action false, lower/upper ports 0.

Use add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. type indicates the top-level type of ACL and takes IPv4 or IPv6, so IPv6 is supported, and it is required at add time. interface references the interface the filter is applied to and accepts 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 or DCN-2-B; run add acl-name interface ? to list the available ones. An ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. name is a string of length 0...30 and admin-state is lock, maintenance or unlock, default unlock. show acl-<name> also returns oper-state and avail-state. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4.

Yes: show access-control-list. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode; it simply displays the access control list. For the individual objects use show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface] for a specific list, and show ace-<name>/<sequence-id> for each access control entry within it. Note that the node's data-model access rules are a different feature, viewed with show access-rule-list-<name> and show access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name>.

Create an access-rule-list bound to that group, then a deny rule inside it. First add access-rule-list-<name> user-group <group>, then add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification or RPC, or an external command, max 255 characters, default *. operation is a bits value of create, read, update, delete, execute (default *), so use 'create update delete' to block writes. module-name defaults to * and description is max 256 characters. Example: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

The access-rule-list is processed in order as given by the sequence-id parameter: lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins. sequence-id is a uint16 and can be changed over the lifetime of the list to re-sort entries; if it is not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, putting the entry at the end of the list. Scope a list to groups with the user-group attribute: add access-rule-list-<name> user-group <value>, a leaf-list of user-group names whose default value * is a match-all meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups. A maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. description is a string of length 0..256. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY.

It is OSPFv3-specific. auth-key adds, edits, shows or deletes the pre-shared key used for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The instance key is add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi>: instance-id is the OSPF instance ID (number, range 0..255), ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID, ospf-if-name references the interface in the OSPF area, and spi is a unique security parameter index for this SA (number, range 256..4294967295). key is the pre-shared key, a string of length 8..128, and type indicates whether the integrity key is ascii or hex encoded. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only: set authorization mode rules-only. The mode values are static-only (only system defined static authorization rules), static+rules (the default: the system looks for a user configured access-rule first and falls back to system rules) and rules-only (only user defined access-rules; if no rule matches, the global defaults apply). Then tighten those defaults, which are only configurable when mode = rules-only: read-default (permit/deny, default permit; covers get/show and receiving notifications), write-default (default deny; covers create/update/delete) and exec-default (default permit; covers RPC invocation and other commands). Set all three to deny for a deny-by-default posture. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications.

A user changes their own password with the operational-mode command password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the current/old and the new password must be given, this is supported only for local users, and a password may contain up to 200 characters. Run password with no arguments for the interactive form: it prompts for the old password, then the new one twice, without echoing, and Ctrl+C cancels. Inline form, usable in scripts: password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!; inline, the double-quote and apostrophe characters must be escaped with a backslash and the characters # ? | ; must be enclosed in single or double quotes. To reset another user's password, an administrator uses set user-<username> force-password-change true, which forces that user to change their password at next login.

show security displays the top level security container. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Beneath it, show security-policies returns the individual policy flags (secure-mode, strict-password-check, minimum-password-length, ssh-authentication-method, default-user-group, password history, AAA methods, SSH and TLS algorithm lists, console-user settings, CRL/OCSP revocation, and the read-only max-system-sessions and max-local-users), while the related security objects have their own commands: user, user-group, user-data, access-rule-list, access-rule, authorization, acl, ace, access-control-list and aaa-server.

Both come from security-policies. minimum-password-length is the configurable minimum length for user passwords: number, range 1..200, default 8; the length is verified against this policy whenever a password is changed. strict-password-check (true/false, default true) additionally enforces a minimum length of 8 characters, at least one lower case letter (a-z), one upper case letter (A-Z), one number (0-9) and one symbol, and forbids the user name being part of the password; when disabled only a minimum length of 1 character is enforced. For reuse, enforce-password-history-check (true/false, default true) ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords, and password-history-size sets the number of passwords stored for reuse checking: number, range 1..200, default 5. These policies only affect newly defined passwords.

Both are per-user attributes of the user command. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive and invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out): number, range 0-255, default 5. suspension-time is the duration of the UID suspension following consecutive invalid login attempts: minutes, range 0 - 1440, default 5. Configure with set user-<user-name> max-invalid-login <value> suspension-time <value>. show user-<user-name> reports user-status, which reads lockout when the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts, and failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login. Lockout can also be turned off globally through the security-policies disable-user-lockout attribute.

show user-data shows the user-data container. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode; the guide lists no attributes for it. For the per-user detail use show user-<user-name>, which can return password, password-hashed, user-group, display-name, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, enabled, user-status, force-password-change, max-sessions, last-login-date, failed-logins, user-aaa-type, alarm-report-control and label.

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. name is the name of the group, a String of 1...64 characters; description is a long description of the user group, a String of 1...128 characters. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them; users are attached to groups via the user-group attribute of the user command. Manage with set user-group-<name> description <value>, show user-group-<name> [description] and delete user-group-<name>. Example: add user-group-XY. The predefined groups shown by show user-group are EA (Encryption Administrator), MA (Monitoring Access), NA (Network Administrator), NE (Network Engineer), PR (Provisioning), SA (Security Administrator) and TT (Turn-up and Test).

Add/Drop Groups are managed with add/set/show/delete adg-<adg-number>. The adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs. Duplication is reported by the read-only show attribute wavelength-duplication: one-per-adg (the default) means no duplication of frequencies in the ADG, and one-per-degree means CDC operation where duplication of frequencies is allowed in the ADG but only one instance at the Degree. Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show-only attributes are max-add-drop-ports (max ports available for the ADG) and bands-supported (not-applicable, standardC-band, superC-band, standardL-band, standardC-standardL-band; default standardC-band). The only settable attribute is label, a string of length 0..256. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: add adg-1

On set amplifier-<name>, gain-target applies in manual control mode and takes 0..40 dB, default 0.0; the actual value in force is shown as gain-operating (0..40 dB, 0.0 when the card is plugged out or the EDFA is disabled). control-mode is auto-max-pw (default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual; in auto mode you do not set gain-target but gain-adjustment, a user offset in the range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, supported only on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: auto (default, system controls tilt per configured fiber parameters), auto-planned (system controls tilt per planning-tool parameters), or manual. So yes, the system controls tilt by itself unless you select manual; when the amplifier function is add or drop the only option is manual. tilt-target applies to manual mode, range [-5..5] dB, default 0 dB, and changing it issues the warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting. tilt-adjustment offsets the target when tilt-control-mode is auto or auto-planned, also [-5..5] dB, default 0 dB. tilt-actual is the measured spectrum tilt.

Use set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with a default of 0 dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different from auto; when control-mode is auto the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (default, you configure only the span attributes and optionally the pointloss), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus the span attributes) and manual (basic manual configuration, where even the target pump powers must be configured). To see how many pumps the card has, use show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps: it is the number of pumps for the required-equipped card, with values 4 or 2, and it dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. Related read-only values are total-pump-power (range [-99..99 dBm], -99 means no power or card not actual), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain, which read 0 when the Raman amplifier or the card is disabled.

Switch it on with set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled, for example: set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled. The attribute can also be supplied on add ase-idler-service-<name>. Values are enabled (ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled) and disabled, which is the default. To see whether it actually came up, read the system-reported ase-idler-state with show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state: ase-enabled means the ASE idler signal filling is complete on the band spectrum, ase-partially-enabled means the filling is incomplete, ase-faulted means the ASE idler signal is faulted, and ase-disabled (the default) means the signal is completely removed from the band spectrum. oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state are also available on show. The function of the object is idler. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On set ase-idler-source-<name>, target-output-power is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured; its range is (-3.00..20.50) dBm and the default is 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled. The read-only pump-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) reports the actual state of the ASE Idler pump. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (0..256 chars) and alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited). The object function is ase-idler-source. Example: set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00'. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the calibrate command: calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type takes raman, which triggers calibration on Raman cards. trigger takes start, which starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span, or stop, which stops it. entity selects the instance to be calibrated; for Raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. Start: calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. Stop: calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. The command is available in Operational Mode only. To follow the run, use show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state, whose values are not-available (never triggered or no prior calibration), in-progress, up-to-date (completed successfully), out-dated (for example due to OTS OLOS or a change in delta pointloss) and fail; additional-info carries troubleshooting text when the state is fail or out-dated, and last-calibration-timestamp defaults to never.

Degrees are created with add degree-<degree-number>; degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node can have up to 20 degrees (show oadm-capabilities max-degrees reports 20). Spectral granularity comes from the show-only attributes: slot-width-granularity, the width of a slot in MHz, default 6250 (6.25 GHz); and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies in MHz, default 3125 (3.125 GHz), computed from the base frequency 193.1 THz per G.694.1. min-slots (default 8) is the minimum number of slots that may be joined to form a media channel and max-slots (default 32) the maximum; min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. bands-supported lists the bands the degree supports, defaulting to standardC-band. Other show attributes are label, is-foadm and wss-less.

Directions on a multi-rail ILA node are indexed 1..16 and are paired per card. Direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. The DWDM Line1 port is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even index value, which is why they come in odd/even pairs. The system sets direction-number from the port you configure: 1 when direction-port is dwdm-line1 and 2 when it is dwdm-line2. So dwdm-line port instances for an odd index must be dwdm-line1 and for an even index must be dwdm-line2, and the same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. direction-card is filled in autonomously as card-<chassis>-<slot>. Example: add direction-1 direction-port port-1-3-dwdm-line1; delete -f direction-1 forces deletion without confirmation. Indexes 1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x.

On a dsc facility you can configure only three things, with add dsc-<name> or set dsc-<name>: label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited). Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. managed-by describes whether the facility was system created or not; its values are system and user, and the default is system. The practical consequence is that only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reported as managed-by system cannot be removed with delete dsc-<name>. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show dsc

On add dsc-group-<name> or set dsc-group-<name> there are two Q signal-degrade thresholds. Pre-FEC: pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 disables threshold-crossing alarming and the specific sub-range depends on the carrier use case; its hysteresis, pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, is 0.1..1.0 dB with a default of 0.5. Post-FEC: post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 12.5..18.0 dB, default 18; post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Alongside these, dgd-high-threshold raises DGD-OORH and is a uint16 in the range 25..400 ps with a default of 100. The mandatory creation parameters are carriers and rate, for example: add dsc-group-1-3-1-1 rate 100 carriers 1-3-1 group-id 1 instance-id 1

Use the gadt command, which retrieves information about golden carrier application information. The syntax is show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>], so there are four application description parameters, H, P, S and U, each a string giving the detailed description of that application ID. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For example, show gadt application-description-H returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application ID letter here is the same one that appears at the end of a carrier mode name such as 800M.95P, whose application field is P.

The gapt command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). It is scoped per card type: the syntax is show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type], where card-type is the card type name, version is the table version (string, length 0..5) and applicable-resource-type names the managed resource type(s) applicable for that particular advanced parameter. Plain show gapt lists the tables with their versions, for example gapt-CHM6 version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 version 3.0 and gapt-CHM7T. Naming a card type, for example show gapt-chm7, lists that card's golden advanced parameters as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<parameter>, such as BOASetting, CRAvgNCtrl, NLC, RxCDMode, RxRollOff and TxSignalBWControl, followed by the table version and applicable-resource-type. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show gcmt, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode; the syntax is show gcmt [<card-type>] [version], where version is the table version. To look up a specific mode, name it: show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P. The output lists the mode with its capacity in Gbps, client-mode, baud-rate in GBaud, application, compatibility-id and status, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view of one mode, including actual-carrier-mode, sop-tracking-mode, supported-subtypes and candidate-subtypes, use show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>. Access for gcmt is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read the status attribute with show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status. status describes the carrier mode release status and takes one of supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated or diagnostic, so a mode is fully supported when status is supported and only experimental when status is experimental. The same field appears in the gcmt table output, for example show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P shows status supported. Per-subtype status is separate: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string 0..32, maximum 20 elements) and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which the carrier mode has candidate status (string 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The carrier-mode key is a string of length 1..15 formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<BaudRate><ApplicationID>, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P.

Use show l0-capabilities. It shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The command takes no parameters at all, and it is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the photonic topology limits specifically, show oadm-capabilities reports max-degrees (20) and max-adgs (110), and show capabilities-<name> retrieves the capabilities of a named card.

A Media Channel is created with add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>, so three things are mandatory: the parent OMS instance identifier and the lower and upper frequencies, both given in MHz. Optional creation parameters are label (0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited) and auto-delete. parent-oms is only set upon MC creation, and the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree; it cannot be in an ADG. The system derives center-frequency (MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete defaults to disabled; when enabled the system deletes the MC once its associated NMC is deleted, and it may only be enabled on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols), being always disabled when l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000'

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command provides only show: show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]. There is no add, set or delete for mc-f, and every attribute is used in show only: name (string 0..64), the XPath references to parent and children facilities, the supporting card and port leafrefs, the AID (string 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, which the system calculates from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency, also in MHz. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]. The index is the card within the ADG and takes a number in the range [1..4], so up to four cards can be put into one Add/Drop Group; the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). adg-number is a number in the range [1..110]. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring takes true or false and defaults to true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example on FOADM nodes. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, at privilege level Network Administrator or Network Engineer. Example: add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6

Use add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>, for example add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. The index is 1 only, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card or subcard belonging to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can change the association with set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>, inspect it with show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card, and remove it with delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, at privilege level Network Administrator or Network Engineer.

Use show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier in MHz as a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, a decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00) with a default of -99; the value -99.00 means no power. The companion attribute monitored-width is the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source or destination, a uint32 in MHz with a default of 0. Both are show-only. Example: show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power, or show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 for all attributes. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On add nmc-<name>, center-frequency is mandatory and is the nominal center frequency of the NMC, with values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. You must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth: the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are only used in add and show, not in set. parent-facility is also mandatory on creation and can be either a Media Channel or an OMS; it is only set upon creation and the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. Example: add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies 75000 MHz (75 GHz) by default: alloc-bandwidth, the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler in MHz units, has a default of 75000. Its allocated span is reported by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency, while actual-lower-frequency, actual-upper-frequency and actual-bandwidth report what is really in place; actual-bandwidth defaults to 0. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, takes enabled or disabled, and because this is a system-created attribute it is enabled by default. Only admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited) can be set with set nmc-f-<name>; everything else, including power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx ([-99.00..99.00] dBm, default -99), is show-only. Example: show nmc-f-1-3-dwdm-line-58

Use show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees and reports 20 (uint8); max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups and reports 110 (uint8). Both report 0 if not supported: degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for the ILA node type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment-supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example output: show oadm-capabilities gives max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110.

On set oc-<name>, the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with a default of none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern injected and takes none (the default), enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 or PRBS31. test-signal-direction is the direction of the test signal and the only value is ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, defaulting to false. All four are settable and readable via show oc-<name>. Example: set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from the OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information; that is, the optical channel monitoring information is derived from the OSC messaging rather than measured per channel locally. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored (as configured by the user) or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Read it with show ochm or show ochm-<name>. Attributes include direction, where only egress is currently supported (default egress), and power-actual, the currently received power in dBm; -99 dBm means the power has not yet been measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card) or no power was detected, or there is no appropriate fiber-connection. For the egress direction the power actual is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, at the same reference point where the target power is defined. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99) and attenuation-actual (0..55 dB) apply to HSC OLS nodes. Only label, admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable.

Use `show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]`. The ocm-channel object lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). It is show-only, in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The key is name (String, length 0..64) plus lower-frequency and upper-frequency (uint32), the lower and upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point). The two reported attributes are opm-pwr, the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 range -99.00..99.00 with default -99, and connected, which yields true if the channel is configured (that is, involved in an oxcon); values true and false, default false.

Yes. On ocm-mp the ocm-enable attribute enables regular power monitoring; values are enabled and disabled, and the default is enabled. Change it with `set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable <value>`; the same set command also takes label (String 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Whether monitoring is actually possible is reported by the read-only monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (enabled/disabled, default enabled). Other read-only attributes are monitored-port, the port being monitored, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM (default not-applicable), and ad-direction, the reference to the AD coupler/splitter DWDM port, which is ingress.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG, and it provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not enabled out of the box: ocm-enable, which enables regular power monitoring, has values enabled and disabled with default disabled. Turn it on with `set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled`. The set command also takes label and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only attributes include ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement, the last OCM scan date and time (default never), adg-number, the ADG reference, uint8 range 0..110, default 0, and monitoring-state, reported as enabled when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible (default disabled).

An OMS defaults to grid-mode flexible, the flexible grid that lets you create and delete MCs of different widths. The other values are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (50 GHz with 88 C-band channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default lower-frequency is 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the section is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive, no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operating with OCM such as a DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization and integrated-equalization. Defaults are intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port belonging to a degree, or on an ILA node.

`set ops-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed), input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role values are tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (the default, used for express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports, in SLTE l0-mode-op) and active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control). Read supported-roles to see which of these the card, and sometimes card-mode, allows. port-expansion is no (default) or y-cable. Example: `set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary`.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency the carrier is tuned to, range 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz, where 0 means not configured; the usable range and step depend on module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz (step 50 MHz), CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz (step 1 MHz), TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, range -55.0..55.00 dBm with per-module limits (CHM2TX -6 to 0, CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0, TOM-400G-C-DWDM -10 to +1), adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm; defaults are CHM2TX 0, CHM7/7X -2, UTM2 -6.0. For a slight trim use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0: it is used for bright tuning, and once set the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes, with `set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled`. When the attribute is set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, and the default is disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card.

Very little. `set optical-channel-<name>` accepts only label (String, length 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), for example `set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock`. Everything else is read-only through `show optical-channel-<name>`: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled or disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

`show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state` reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state, values enabled and disabled, default disabled. It is read-only and only of relevance for DWDM line ports: on RD amplifiers it reflects the source (Tx) pump, on Raman modules the pump laser. Yes, you can add fixed pad on the receive side: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB is equivalent to no fixed attenuator, for example `set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10`. There is a matching fix-tx-attenuation after port Tx with the same range and default, but it is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured powers are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx, -99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm.

The decision uses the LOS/Signal Fail thresholds on optical-switch, and they are settable. working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold define the Signal Fail (SF) threshold for the working and protection path, optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm, default -23 dBm each. facility-los-threshold is the facility port threshold, power below it leads to loss of signal, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, also -55.0 to 0 dBm, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only happens when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). los-threshold-hysteresis defaults to 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis to 2 dB, both decimal64 range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in steps of 0.1 dB; 1 dB is recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

`set osc-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed), l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6 (ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS). osc-control is auto (default) or manual; HSC OLS nodes support auto only. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, na (default) or -2.5..4.5 dBm. tx-power-adjustment is na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is 0..30 dB, default 10, used in manual control mode. lof-soak-timer is short (default, about 3 ms) or long (about 2300 ms) and is visible only for the PBAx card. monitoring-mode, oscc-support, osc-mode and osc-wavelength are read-only.

Use `show otdr-<name> otdr-state`. It indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification. Values are not-available (status is not available, the default), idle, measuring (measurement is ongoing), finished (measurement has completed) and fail (measurement has failed). When a measurement ends with an error, otdr-error carries the error message. Supporting read-only attributes are otdr-measurement-time, the time remaining in the current measurement (default 0), otdr-laser-state (not-available, enabled, disabled), otdr-measurement-port (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction (not-available, tx, rx) and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile (none, short, medium, long, raman-precheck1, raman-precheck2, raman-precheck3).

Tune these on otdr-ptp with add or set. otdr-range specifies the distance range in km used to calculate the measurement repetition period; values auto (default) or 0...300.0 km, and it is recommended to set the actual fiber length plus 10 percent. From R9.1, if the corresponding OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, otdr-range is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10 percent margin, rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (15 s), slow (1 min), precision (3 to 5 min), high-precision (5 to 7 min) or auto (default). Also settable: otdr-ior (auto or 1.0...2.0), peak-power (auto or 5...14.5) and launching-fiber-length (0...50 m, default 0, auto not supported).

On the OTS facility. `set ots-<name>` takes fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both defaulting to SSMF, with values AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor (fiber-type-rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx are auto (default) or 0..500.0 km, required for tilt control and, for rx, when Raman backward pumping is deployed. Loss is declared with span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 range 0..80 dB (span-loss-receive also allows 99 dB as not configured), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Additional loss such as patch panel goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx, 0..30 dB, default 0. span-loss-reference selects configured or measured (default measured).

The system generates it. The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning, in the format 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>'. So an RD20TM DWDM line terminating an OTS section is addressed as `show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line`, and C2ILASGH lines as ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. Only nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled or enabled, default disabled) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters/bytes) are user-settable. tx-operator is likewise automatically defaulted by the system, with the format '<ne-name>-<Dxx>', giving <ne-name>-D00.

ots-r assumes SSMF. required-fiber-type-rx is the required fiber type on the DWDM line with reference to the Rx fiber, default SSMF, with values AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor; it is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and when there is no fiber-connection. About the receive span you can also declare fiber-length-rx (unspecified by default, or 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (default 99), external-attenuation-rx, and delta-pointloss, the additional Rx attenuation that can be determined after turning up pumps, for example from a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx; values not-applicable (default) or -1..3.5 dB. `set ots-r-<name>` also takes label, admin-state and alarm-report-control, as in `set ots-r-11-2-dwdm-line external-attenuation-rx 2`.

Yes, and the default depends on the deployment. automatic-otdr on ots-r-auto-otdr enables or disables the OTDR based automatic fiber check; values enabled and disabled, with the default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with integrated OTDR the default is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it while a test is in progress aborts the ongoing OTDR test and lets the amplifier blocked by the automatic OTDR be activated. Progress is read from auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail or aborted. Example: `set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled`.

Use add with the mandatory source and destination endpoints, for example `add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'`. Optional on add: label, activation-mode, auto-delete, activation-request-fwd/bwd, direction (two-way default, or one-way), target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst (decimal64, -18.00..15.00 dBm) and circuit-id. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated automatically by the system on creation and deactivated on deletion, and that is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation. In SLTE mode the default is manual and in HSC OLS mode activate-on-create; there you drive it with activation-request-fwd/bwd (no-request, activate, deactivate) and watch activation-state-fwd/bwd.

profile-control applies only to the RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul. It is an Operational mode command: `profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]`. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity references the OMS or NMC; direction is tx or rx, and for power-profile only tx is supported. For RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. The OMS attenuation string is '<StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...', attenuation 0 - 25.50, with N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz granularity; NMC attenuation allows -10 - 25.50 and N cannot exceed 32.

Not much. `set pump-<name>` accepts only label (String, length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else is read-only through `show pump-<name>`: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user; only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. To change the power of a Raman pump use the pump-power command and its target-pump-power attribute instead.

Use `set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>`, where pump-id is an integer identifying the number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power required in dBm and applies when the control-mode is manual; values are -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable, which is the default, and 0 is the not-applicable case. On an RPBM card the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) alarm is raised. Read the permitted limits with `show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power`, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows what is programmed in hardware (derived automatically if control-mode is auto), and actual-pump-power the measured value, default -99.

Use `show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state`, for example `show raman-calibration-1-8`. calibration-state displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (calibration has not been triggered, or no prior calibration has occurred; this is the default), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and up to date), out-dated (out of date due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) and fail (ended with a failure). last-calibration-timestamp gives when the automatic Raman gain calibration rpc last completed, with or without errors; default never. When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info holds troubleshooting information. gain-calibration-error is the residual gain error after each iteration in dB, and calibrated-delta-pointloss the suggested delta-pointloss, -3..3.5 dB.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. `set rsc-<name>` accepts label, admin-state (Unlock, Locked, Maintenance, Unknown; default Unlocked) and alarm-report-control (Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed). `show rsc-<name>` reports the pilot tone powers: rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. It also shows supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled, default enabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user created facilities can be user deleted). Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the OMS underneath is not in a monitoring mode that creates one. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer OMS monitoring-mode is configured as either non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of this managed object depends on the OMS monitoring-mode. The object spectrum is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Once present, dge-in-use reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization (default false), and attenuation-setting gives a unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum, range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw.

Use spectrum-control, which is keyed by name, direction and center-frequency: `set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1`. direction is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported (default egress); center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and it is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer or equivalent is in use (dge-in-use = 'true'). target-output-power is the intended target output power, not-specified by default or in the range -55..55 dBm. Read back attenuation-actual, readable only when a DGE is in use, and width, the detected width from spectrum-monitoring in MHz, which returns 0 if the frequency does not match or if no ILAx card or no DGE is fiber-connected.

Use the read-only spectrum-monitoring command: show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual], for example show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750. It is available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. name is a string 0..64; direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. lower-frequency and upper-frequency give the Media Channel edges in MHz. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99; -99dBm means the power has not yet been measured by the OCM at the DGE2 card, or no power was detected (or there is no appropriate fiber-connection). For egress, power-actual is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, the same reference point where target power is defined. target-actual-power is the power calculated by ATPS, default -99dBm, and is only relevant when target-power-setting = auto. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz with 2 digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on the spectral width.

Read the contention-check-status attribute of the super-channel. It is settable on add (add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [contention-check-status]) and readable with show super-channel-<name> contention-check-status. The Contention Check state is set via DNA in openwave mode and takes the values pending, success, overridden and failk, with default pending. It is only applicable if openwave-contention-check is enabled at the super-channel-group level; openwave-contention-check enables the DNA assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode, takes true or false and defaults to false. So enable openwave-contention-check on the super-channel-group first (add -m super-channel-group-<name> ... openwave-contention-check <value>), otherwise the status stays meaningless. The related line-system-mode indicates the L1 to L0 power control mode and is openwave. Both commands run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

-m is the merge flag: 'Merge configuration (the command will not fail if the entity already exists)'. The add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only, so the -m flag is required. A merge is a best effort add: if the target entity does not exist it is created, and if it already exists it is updated with whatever attributes are present on the add command. The full form is add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]. Defaults are admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, line-system-mode openwave and valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200). The same -m merge flag applies to comm-channel.
